content.user_title: Mine Search Terms for Better Keywords
content.value_statement: Paid search reports can hide profitable queries and wasted spend. This skill turns an export into keyword, negative-keyword, and n-gram actions.
actual_capabilities: Checks that a search-terms export includes query, cost, and conversion data.
Identifies converting queries for new keywords or matching ad groups.
Flags high-spend, zero-conversion queries for negative keywords.
Builds one-word, two-word, and three-word waste rankings from non-converting queries.
Produces add, negate, and move recommendations with stated thresholds.
Summarizes spend-efficiency evidence for a later account audit.
limitations: Requires a user-provided export or pasted report with reliable query, cost, and conversion fields.
Does not connect to ad platforms or apply changes in an advertising account.
Does not design account structure, allocate budgets, or calculate the final account score.
Recommendations need human review for match type, business relevance, and conversion quality.

use_cases.title: Weekly negative-keyword review
use_cases.description: Find costly, non-converting queries and prepare negatives with proposed match types.

use_cases.title: Convert query winners into keywords
use_cases.description: Route converting search queries to new keywords or suitable ad groups.

use_cases.title: Diagnose recurring wasted spend
use_cases.description: Rank non-converting query tokens by measured cost to reveal recurring waste themes.

prompt_templates.title: Start with an export
prompt_templates.prompt: Mine this search-terms export. Identify converting queries to add and costly non-converting queries to negate.

prompt_templates.title: Build a negative list
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this search-terms report. Use a stated cost threshold and create a negative-keyword list with proposed match types.

prompt_templates.title: Find waste patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a one-word, two-word, and three-word n-gram waste report from these non-converting search terms. Rank each by measured cost.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a maintenance diff
prompt_templates.prompt: For this direct-response search-terms export, produce add, negate, and move actions. State thresholds, label measured values, and flag decisions that need approval.

output_examples.input: A search-terms export with cost and conversion columns.
output: Add: “winter running gloves” as a keyword because it produced conversions.
Negate: “free running gloves” as a phrase negative after meaningful spend and zero conversions.
Review: “free” is a high-cost n-gram and may need a shared negative list.

output_examples.input: A weekly report for a prospecting campaign.
output: Maintenance summary with query counts, stated thresholds, and measured spend.
A ranked n-gram waste list and proposed ad-group or campaign negative levels.

best_practices: Use a recent export that includes query, cost, conversions, and conversion value when available.
Set and state a cost threshold before recommending negative keywords.
Review proposed negatives against product intent before applying them.
anti_patterns: Do not negate queries based on clicks alone when conversion data is missing.
Do not treat estimated metrics as measured export values.
Do not use this skill to redesign campaigns or allocate budgets.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide search query, cost, and conversions. Conversion value is useful for ROAS analysis.

faq.question: Can it access my advertising account?
faq.answer: No. It uses a pasted report or a user-provided export and does not apply account changes.

faq.question: Does it create negative keywords automatically?
faq.answer: No. It proposes negatives and match types for human review.

faq.question: What is an n-gram waste report?
faq.answer: It ranks recurring one-word, two-word, and three-word query tokens by non-converting spend.

faq.question: Can it identify new keywords?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies converting queries that may become keywords or fit existing ad groups.

faq.question: How often should I run it?
faq.answer: Run it weekly or monthly, depending on query volume and campaign change frequency.
